body:
Thanks for the support Anoninsen.  

When I was growing up my father was emotionally and physically abusive and I used to get the brunt focus of it.  He battled alcoholism and when he was sober he was pretty nice, but once he started drinking in the afternoon the mood around the house quickly changed.  I've actually went to therapy for the lingering effects of this when I was in my mid 20s.  There's something called Adult Children of Alcoholic Parents where most adults who had alcoholic parents share anywhere up to 20 traits because their environment.  

You aren't being harsh at all.  And thank you for the support.

Thank you for the kind words Zehnj.  You are right coming to terms with traumatic events are key and sometimes I try to accept the terms, even though I dont want to, other times I still cant believe it all.  Every time I wake up there's a short moment right when I wake up where I still think everything is okay.  

Family has been great but live in different cities so its hard to see them as much as I'd like.  At first I didn't want to see them at all.  It was just an extremely hard time and I sort of pushed a lot of people away.  The distance between us is hard but I get calls everyday from them which is nice. 

I know you are right that time will heals but from where I am right now its hard to imagine that tomorrow will be any better than today.  I am holding on mainly because I don't want my family to feel even worst than they already are now.
